definition: a stone coffin, often carved or inscribed, used for a burial
hook: A sarcophagus was named for what it did to the body.
modernAnchor: Museum halls, Egyptian tombs, a carved stone box with a lid. We call it a sarcophagus.
journey: Greeks quarried a limestone near Assos that was said to dissolve a corpse within weeks.
They called the stone lithos sarkophagos, flesh-eating stone, from sarx, flesh, and phagein, to eat.
Coffins carved from that stone took the name, and the phrase shrank to just the second half.
Rome and later Europe kept the word for any grand stone coffin, long after the legend stopped mattering.
